summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (P32) framing a research hypothesis ("assumption-kill") about whether bradykinin retains residual phenotype (nociception, plasma extravasation, neurogenic inflammation) under B2R genetic loss-of-function (Bdkrb2 KO) or B2R-matched antagonism (HOE-140/icatibant-class) that abolishes B2R-class attribution. The document is a pre-registered discussion card, not a completed experiment; the key experimental outcome (matched residual bradykinin under Bdkrb2/HOE abolish) is explicitly marked EMPTY/UNKNOWN. Supporting prior art from four published studies (Griesbacher 1987, Wirth 1991, Hess 1992, Borkowski 1995) establishes BK phenotype, B2R antagonist tools, receptor identity, and genetic LOF necessity — all pointing against residual phenotype rather than supporting it.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis / Claim (P32) — Bradykinin Residual Phenotype Under B2R Abolish
content_blocks.content: The central claim (P32) asks whether bradykinin retains residual phenotype ≥50% of bradykinin-alone (or bradykinin vs vehicle Δ) on B2R-intact concurrent controls under conditions that abolish B2R-class nociception/plasma-extravasation/neurogenic-inflammation attribution via Bdkrb2 genetic LOF or B2R-matched antagonism (HOE-140/icatibant-class). This is framed as an 'assumption-kill' / 'bdkrb2-insufficiency' test. The claim requires: (1) a pre-registered acute/subacute rodent panel (Griesbacher/Wirth/Hess/Borkowski-class); (2) a bradykinin-alone arm on B2R-intact concurrent controls; (3) a B2R-abolish condition confirmed to eliminate B2R-class attribution; (4) a bradykinin-under-abolish arm scored against the intact-arm comparator. Polarity is NEGATIVE; status is NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art #1 — Griesbacher 1987 (PMID 3479223)
content_blocks.content: Griesbacher et al. (Br J Pharmacol 1987; PMID 3479223; DOI 10.1111/j.1476-5381.1987.tb11328.x; PMC1853661) maps BK phenotype PRIOR: plasma extravasation, nociceptor stimulation, PGE2 release, venoconstriction in rabbit models using B4310-class antagonists. Antagonist arms demonstrate necessity of B2R-class signaling AGAINST residual phenotype. Document explicitly notes: 'occlusion ≠ residual-retain.' This is classified as LITERATURE evidence; assay type = rabbit plasma extravasation / venoconstriction / PGE2 / nociceptor / iris sphincter. No residual-positive H2H arm present.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art #2 — Wirth 1991 (PMID 1364852)
content_blocks.content: Wirth et al. (Br J Pharmacol 1991; PMID 1364852; DOI 10.1111/j.1476-5381.1991.tb12249.x; PMC1917928) characterizes Hoe 140 as a potent, long-acting B2R antagonist in vivo. Assays: rat BK hypotensive responses; guinea-pig BK bronchoconstriction; carrageenin paw oedema; dog tolerability. Hoe 140 inhibits BK hypotensive/bronchoconstriction/carrageenin oedema. Classified as B2R antagonist TOOL (not a residual H2H study). Provides the pharmacological tool for the proposed P32 abolish-gate but does not itself demonstrate residual bradykinin phenotype under B2R abolish.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art #3 — Hess 1992 (PMID 1314587)
content_blocks.content: Hess et al. (Biochem Biophys Res Commun 1992; PMID 1314587; DOI 10.1016/0006-291x(92)91187-u) reports cloning and pharmacological characterization of the human bradykinin BK-2 receptor (Bdkrb2). Method: human BK-2 receptor cDNA cloning; mammalian cell expression; pharmacological characterization consistent with BK-2 subtype. Conclusion: cloned receptor is a G protein-coupled human bradykinin (BK-2) receptor. Classified as Bdkrb2 identity FOUNDATION / necessity-leaning BK→B2R attribution. Document cautions: 'do not invent KD/IC50 from abstract as scout measurements.' BK is confirmed as endogenous B2R ligand; residual under B2R abolish would imply a non-B2R bridge.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art #4 — Borkowski 1995 (PMID 7775424)
content_blocks.content: Borkowski et al. (J Biol Chem 1995; PMID 7775424; DOI 10.1074/jbc.270.23.13706) reports targeted disruption of the B2 bradykinin receptor gene (Bdkrb2 KO). Assays: ileum, uterus, superior cervical ganglia preparations. Result: homozygous Bdkrb2 KO mice are fertile; BK fails to produce responses in smooth muscle and neurons. Classified as Bdkrb2 genetic LOF TOOL + necessity AGAINST residual. Document explicitly states: 'BK action eliminated = necessity, NOT residual-positive BK-in-KO; do NOT misread as residual+.' This is the strongest necessity-against-residual evidence in the prior art set.

content_blocks.title: Key Experimental Gap — Matched Residual H2H (EMPTY/UNKNOWN)
content_blocks.content: The critical prediction variable 'matched_residual_bradykinin_under_Bdkrb2_HOE_abolish_H2H' is explicitly marked EMPTY/UNKNOWN. No published study has been identified that provides a clean residual-positive bradykinin arm under Bdkrb2 LOF or HOE-140/icatibant-class abolish on a nociception/plasma-extravasation/neurogenic-inflammation panel with bradykinin-alone on B2R-intact concurrent controls as the named comparator. Soft-complete scores: Q_resid_tight=21 all NON-MATCH; Q_resid_life_h2h=2 NON-MATCH; Q_bk_in_ko inflated without clean exogenous-BK retain; Q_necess necessity AGAINST (Borkowski/Wirth/Griesbacher/Hess). Document states: 'soft-complete empty ≠ novelty / ≠ failure.'

content_blocks.title: Prediction Variables and Thresholds
content_blocks.content:
Six prediction variables are defined:
1. Griesbacher_BK_phenotype_plus_antagonist_necessity — LITERATURE; threshold: B4310-class antagonists inhibit BK-induced plasma extravasation, venoconstriction, PGE2, nociceptor stimulation (PMID 3479223); occlusion ≠ residual-retain.
2. Wirth_HOE140_B2R_antagonist_tool_not_residual — LITERATURE; threshold: Hoe 140 inhibits BK hypotensive/bronchoconstriction/carrageenin oedema (PMID 1364852); not residual H2H.
3. Hess_Bdkrb2_identity_BK_is_B2R_ligand — LITERATURE; threshold: cloned receptor is G protein-coupled human BK-2 receptor (PMID 1314587); BK IS endogenous B2R ligand.
4. Borkowski_Bdkrb2_KO_necessity_AGAINST_residual — LITERATURE; threshold: BK fails to produce responses in smooth muscle and neurons in Bdkrb2 KO (PMID 7775424); necessity AGAINST residual.
5. matched_residual_bradykinin_under_Bdkrb2_HOE_abolish_H2H — UNKNOWN; threshold: dedicated residual-positive BK phenotype under Bdkrb2 LOF/HOE-140 abolish on Griesbacher/Wirth/Hess/Borkowski-style panels — EMPTY.
6. residual_bradykinin_phenotype_ge_50pct_of_alone_when_B2R_class_abolished — PREDICTION; threshold: residual BK phenotype ≥50% of BK-alone (or BK vs vehicle Δ) on B2R-intact concurrent controls under Bdkrb2 LOF or HOE-140/icatibant abolish; α/N pre-specified; author-chosen prediction, not observed.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Experimental Design (Primary Kill Path)
content_blocks.content: Primary kill path: pre-registered acute/subacute rodent (Griesbacher/Wirth/Hess/Borkowski-class) nociception/plasma-extravasation/neurogenic-inflammation panel. Required arms: (A) bradykinin-alone (or bradykinin vs vehicle) on B2R-intact concurrent controls; (B) Bdkrb2 genetic LOF or B2R-matched antagonism (HOE-140/icatibant-class) with block QC confirming abolition of B2R-class attribution; (C) bradykinin-under-abolish arm scored against arm A. Preferred sequence: cell/SPR/block-QC with HOE-140/icatibant-class or Bdkrb2 ablation BEFORE new animal panels. Refute condition: residual BK phenotype <50% of BK-alone/intact-arm Δ when abolish-gate, BK-alone/intact comparator, and power/assay artifacts are ruled out. Competing inconclusive outcomes: abolish-fail, BK-null, underpowered strata, assay-mismatch, B1-panel mismatch without selective confirmation.

content_blocks.title: B1 Receptor (Bdkrb1) Honesty Caveat
content_blocks.content: The document acknowledges a B1 receptor (Bdkrb1) honesty caveat (Q_B1=90; reference: PMID 8552260 — inflammation modulates B1 vs B2). Instruction: document B1 as a caveat ONLY; do NOT promote B1 as residual-positive under B2 abolish; do not invent residual+ from B1 literature. B1 mismatch is listed as a pre-registered competing inconclusive outcome (not a refute outcome).

content_blocks.title: Series Distinctness / Skip-List Discipline
content_blocks.content: P32 is explicitly distinguished from P15–P31 (all NON-MATCH). Critical non-matches: P30 (CGRP/RAMP1; BK≠CGRP; Bdkrb2≠RAMP1; Q_P30_tight=0) and P31 (Substance P/NK1R; BK≠SP; Bdkrb2≠Tacr1; Q_P31_tight=1). Also distinct from: P29 orexin/OX1R, P28 VIP/VPAC2, P27 NPY/Y1, P26 PACAP/PAC1, P25 ghrelin/GHSR, P24 GLP1R, P23 OXTR, P22 Dihexa/c-Met, P21 Selank/GABA, P20 Semax/TrkB, P19 ARA290/IRR, P18 SS-31/ROS, P17 MOTS-c/folate, P16 LKKTETQ-Cc, P15 residual-FBXO22. NOT FOXO4×LOF (SERIES_FROZEN). orthosteric_drift=false.

content_blocks.content: execution_status=NOT_RUN. fto_status=UNKNOWN. kill_cost_tier=1. time_to_refute=4 weeks. ip_class=bdkrb2-insufficiency. vault_hold=no. Status labels: NEGATIVE. Polarity: negative. Risk class: research-discussion. The document is a pre-registered discussion card pending dual-publish; no experimental data has been generated for P32.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis — What Collapses Without Key Design Elements
content_blocks.content:
Three ablation conditions are described:
1. Remove matched nociception/plasma-extravasation/neurogenic-inflammation panel with BK-alone on B2R-intact concurrent controls ± Bdkrb2 LOF or HOE-140/icatibant under B2R-abolish: without this, separate Griesbacher/Wirth/Hess/Borkowski literature cannot show bdkrb2-insufficiency of residual BK.
2. Remove B2R-abolish gate plus BK-alone/intact-arm comparator: without this, the card collapses into generic B2R-class framing and loses bdkrb2-insufficiency contrast.
3. Remove P15≠P32 through P31≠P32 discipline plus BK-is-B2R-ligand honesty and B1-caveat-not-invented-residual: treating prior series or empty PubMed as deciding residual-under-Bdkrb2-abolish would invent an H2H result left EMPTY/UNKNOWN.

key_findings: P32 is a pre-registered hypothesis (NOT_RUN) asking whether bradykinin retains residual phenotype ≥50% of BK-alone under Bdkrb2 genetic LOF or HOE-140/icatibant-class B2R antagonism that abolishes B2R-class nociception/plasma-extravasation/neurogenic-inflammation attribution.
The matched residual H2H experimental outcome is explicitly EMPTY/UNKNOWN — no published study provides a clean residual-positive BK arm under Bdkrb2/HOE abolish on the required panel design.

Four prior art studies (Griesbacher 1987, Wirth 1991, Hess 1992, Borkowski 1995) collectively establish BK phenotype, B2R antagonist tools, receptor identity, and genetic LOF necessity — all pointing AGAINST residual phenotype rather than supporting it.
Borkowski 1995 (PMID 7775424): Bdkrb2 KO eliminates BK action in smooth muscle and neurons — strongest necessity-against-residual evidence; explicitly not to be misread as residual-positive.
Griesbacher 1987 (PMID 3479223): B4310-class antagonists inhibit BK-induced plasma extravasation, venoconstriction, PGE2 release, nociceptor stimulation — occlusion ≠ residual-retain.

Wirth 1991 (PMID 1364852): Hoe 140 is a potent long-acting B2R antagonist in vivo (rat hypotension, guinea-pig bronchoconstriction, carrageenin oedema) — pharmacological tool, not a residual H2H study.
Hess 1992 (PMID 1314587): Cloning and pharmacological characterization of human BK-2 receptor (Bdkrb2) — BK confirmed as endogenous B2R ligand; residual under B2R abolish would imply non-B2R bridge.
B1 receptor (Bdkrb1) acknowledged as honesty caveat (Q_B1=90; PMID 8552260) but explicitly not to be promoted as residual-positive under B2 abolish.

Refute condition: residual BK phenotype <50% of BK-alone/intact-arm Δ when abolish-gate and power/assay artifacts are ruled out — would confirm B2R-class sufficiency and kill bdkrb2-insufficiency hypothesis.
Execution status: NOT_RUN; kill_cost_tier=1; estimated time_to_refute=4 weeks; FTO status UNKNOWN.
P32 is explicitly distinct from P15–P31 (all NON-MATCH), especially P30 (CGRP/RAMP1) and P31 (Substance P/NK1R); NOT FOXO4×LOF (SERIES_FROZEN).
